dedupe_keys.name: living breakwaters tottenville staten island rebuild by design

description: Living Breakwaters is a nature-based coastal protection project on the south shore of Staten Island at Tottenville, New York City, one of the areas hardest hit by Hurricane Sandy, where dredging and the loss of oyster reefs had left the shore exposed to waves and erosion. Designed by SCAPE Landscape Architecture with Parsons Brinckerhoff, Stevens Institute of Technology and others, and implemented by the Governor's Office of Storm Recovery, it places eight partly submerged breakwaters, about 2,400 feet in all, some 1,000 feet offshore, built of marine stone and ecologically enhanced concrete with reef ridges and tide pool units that give habitat to oysters and other marine life, and it works with the Tottenville dune plantings as layered protection. The design team ran hydrodynamic modelling and engineering analysis to choose design scenarios, reviewed with a Citizens Advisory Committee. Construction began in September 2021 and was completed in 2024; the page gives a 60 million dollar Rebuild by Design CDBG-DR award and a total of 107 to 111 million dollars. The project page is accessible online as free HTML, with the original proposal as a PDF. Caveats: the page quotes two different totals, and monitored performance data are not published there. It illustrates simulation-backed nature-based storm surge, wave and erosion hazard reduction for climate adaptation; related records are the Sand Motor and Hesketh Out Marsh case studies.
